answer: A Sybil-resistant economy can require each agent identity to lock a meaningful, time-vested deposit before it can transact at full trust: the deposit acts as quartz in the system foundation, hard to fake at scale, while reputation accrues only slowly, like a glacier, so a fresh identity cannot instantly reach the zenith of trust. Creating a thousand fake identities then means locking a thousand deposits and waiting through the same slow thaw, which makes mass forgery expensive while honest newcomers can still earn standing over time.
